questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Fit snugly.
Be uncomfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Focus only on your controls and not look ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, make yourself visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to stay visible. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where you are most likely to be seen in the driver's rearview mirror.

questions.question: Wind noise while riding:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.
Can permanently damage your hearing.
Is never dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can cause permanent hearing loss. Use ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: If you drink just one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you should:

options.text: Not wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors to stay visible, even in daylight.

questions.question: You have been drinking. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. Your abilities and judgment may still be impaired even if you wait.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside, move to another lane to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for passengers. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol quickly causes it to build up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after that hour.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.

options.text: Tailgating
Honking the horn incorrectly
Communicating with other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgating
questions.explanation: Following too closely, called "tailgating," is a major cause of motorcycle collisions. When riding behind another vehicle, keep a safe distance.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should only be used on slippery roads.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: If hazards are to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?

options.text: Right
Left
Either side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space possible. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire suddenly went flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
You see air coming out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Avoid riding directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chance of an accident by:

options.text: Not looking ahead for hazards.
Not using turn signals to avoid distracting other drivers.
Being visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, make yourself visible, signal your intentions clearly, keep safe distance, watch ahead, and spot hazards. Always be ready to react to any hazard.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Get off the road.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced by:

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Riding more slowly.
Reading the owner's manual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injury is always a risk when riding, no matter your speed. A quality helmet worn properly greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injury.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, how does your ability to safely ride change?

options.text: It gets better.
It stays the same.
It gets worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets worse.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink alcohol. Do not ride if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work well?

options.text: Fasten securely to your head.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Prevent you from wearing eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely to your head.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should also be scratch-free, let you see clearly to the sides, allow air to pass through, and fit over glasses if needed.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When there are at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there are at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you look for when scanning the area around your motorcycle?

options.text: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
Whether you can travel faster than other vehicles.
Pedestrians to stare at.

questions.correctAnswerText: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes in or around intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones while scanning for hazards.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to increase space ahead.
Ignore them.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to increase space ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that lets the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: What should you do if bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see?

options.text: Keep using your mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell drivers about your turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your mechanical signals hard to see. It is important to communicate clearly with other drivers.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection in a crash?

options.text: Denim
Leather or synthetic materials
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Sturdy leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in a crash. Wear long pants and jackets when riding.

questions.question: How should you load a motorcycle's saddlebags?

options.text: Put equal weight in each bag.
Put more weight in one bag than the other.
Put as much weight as possible in one bag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put equal weight in each bag.
questions.explanation: Load both saddlebags with about the same weight. Uneven weight will cause your motorcycle to drift to one side.

questions.question: How can you reduce the chance of a collision?

options.text: Look straight ahead only.
Do not move to avoid hazards.
Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead on your path of travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead on your path of travel.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead as you ride. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.
